sections: Estimated benefit, actual fee and action selection
blockers.finding: Tie priority and strict keep hurdle can disagree when a target above the hurdle is within epsilon of an active target below the hurdle. Pairwise epsilon ties also need an anchor because approximate equality is not transitive.
blockers.requested_edit: Specify deterministic order: latch first; score all allowed targets; filter targets with S > CE_keep + epsilon; if empty keep; let M be maximum eligible target score; among eligible scores with M-S <= epsilon choose active, defensive, central, growth-tilted. Evaluate strict hurdle on the chosen target too. Define ties relative to M, never a sequential pairwise comparator.
blockers.synthetic_evidence: epsilon_tie_gate_ambiguity in verification.json shows keep=1, active=1+0.75 epsilon, defensive=1+1.5 epsilon: priority-first keeps while eligible-first trades.

blockers.finding: Paired median gain is explicit, but p10 decline and p90 loss increase do not explicitly distinguish differences of marginal quantiles from quantiles of paired differences. The current-simplest comparator and adaptive eligibility when context fails are not operationally explicit. Adaptive-versus-balanced_cost rows are needed to apply the second control but not expressly listed among additional paired outputs.
blockers.requested_edit: Declare gain=median_s(CAGR_alt-CAGR_ref); tail growth difference=Q10(CAGR_alt)-Q10(CAGR_ref), required >= -0.10 pp/year; loss difference=Q90(DD_alt)-Q90(DD_ref), required <=1.00 pp; fold count uses strictly positive median_s paired gains within each fold at H=30. Declare explicit adaptive comparator list [balanced_context,balanced_cost], and whether adaptive may qualify when context fails its own promotion gate (recommended yes only if both direct comparisons pass). Require all three incremental paired contrasts, including adaptive-cost, both fees. Declare primary promotion and doubled-fee robustness separately; no retuning.
blockers.synthetic_evidence: paired_vs_marginal_statistics shows opposite median comparisons and very different paired-tail versus marginal-tail differences.

sections: Estimated benefit, actual fee and action selection
limitations.finding: Gamma=4, buffer=2 and coarse targets are normative model choices, not estimated preferences or demonstrated optima. One-year marginal CE can be transparent for a limited competition pilot; it cannot optimize long-horizon drawdown, guarantee gain, establish causality, identify personal risk aversion, or predict unseen tail events.
limitations.requested_edit: Retain disclosures; add within-scenario dependence and pooled-regime/exchangeability caveats. CE weights bad one-year gross factors heavily; confirm numerical rejection rather than clipping.

sections: Customer suitability: separate horizon, willingness and liquidity checks
limitations.finding: All five profiles have their own correct horizon. Horizon and reserve are simultaneous eligibility conditions: A/E Conservative only; B Conservative/Balanced; C all three; D Conservative/Balanced because Growth fails the medium-liquidity reserve despite H=25. These are service assumptions, not calibrated financial laws; bill reserve may drift and is not a cash guarantee.
limitations.requested_edit: Encode allowed class sets explicitly in handoff/config to avoid interpreting cap strings as an exclusive class. Preserve own horizons, willingness and liquidity vetoes; disclose no withdrawals/intraperiod cash stress.

sections: Customer suitability: separate horizon, willingness and liquidity checks
limitations.finding: P90 drawdown can pass with losses above tolerance and p10 nonnegative CAGR is a terminal lower-tail screen, not path protection or a 90% future probability guarantee. Median optimization can select weak severe tails, though only three menus and a lower-growth 0.10 pp indifference rule reduce false precision.
limitations.requested_edit: Keep complete screens including excluded candidates, exceedance fraction with denominator, median/severe loss, p10 growth and reason codes. Use inclusive <= tolerance, >=0 p10 and <=0.10 pp gap. Report sampling uncertainty without claiming significance or treating annual training rows as independent scenarios.

sections: Human review and holdings while pending
Customer suitability: separate horizon, willingness and liquidity checks
limitations.finding: 25% is a generic normative suspension trigger, not each profile tolerance or a loss cap. Prefix maximum drawdown persists even after recovery. Suspension preserves current component dollars at review, then assets still earn returns; it cannot reverse losses or liquidate exposure. Personalized thresholds may change outcomes either way.
limitations.requested_edit: Mandatory separate own-tolerance rerun and risk/purchasing-power rescreen at own H before freeze. State whether a failed provisional class causes referral or reselection; minimally retain prescribed referral without unregistered fallback searches. Keep generic H=30 comparisons separate; do not assume personalized overlay improves results. Define human-review share as latched action-years/review-years and report first latch separately.

limitations.finding: Four evaluation folds exclude the entire matching fold from all training and fitting. Context modes have identical prior/prefix data and 15:n mixture, but their holdings, review latches and targets can diverge. Equal information schedule does not mean equal state. Prefix updating is an assumed predictive mechanism, not evidence of predictability.
limitations.requested_edit: Hash sorted training/evaluation IDs and exact ordered training factors; keep calibrations immutable and shared across both fees. Test all fold exclusions and no future/current observations. Explain overlapping fold training and design selection prevent interpreting OOF as an untouched test or independent fold significance.

limitations.finding: Baseline summaries were already viewed and multiple modes/fees/horizons are examined. Predeclared thresholds mitigate further selection but cannot remove researcher choices or hindsight. Context-cost isolates updating; adaptive-context is essential to attribute value to changing targets. Reference-only outperformance is insufficient.
limitations.requested_edit: Preserve all 16 mode-fee outcomes, failed attempts, fold differences and all primary/robustness decisions; do not promote by choosing the fee or horizon that looks best. At k=.005 regenerate baseline accounting at that fee; reuse audited k=.0025 references only with exact source/config/input identity.

Implementation and output handoff after design acceptance
limitations.finding: The text allows tiny nominal rebalance requests to be counted as nontrade. Clarify execution versus reporting so epsilon never erases actual fees or silently changes active targets. A single initial-deferred flag cannot explain retries versus postdeployment keeps.
limitations.requested_edit: Keep exact accounting even for a tiny accepted request; trade-count threshold is reporting only. Define active_target_before/after and target update only on accepted executed request; no update on rejected proposal or review. Define initial_allocation_deferred as year-1 nondeployment and add per-review reason plus first deployment year/null; keep exact dollars when gate fails.

sections: Implementation and output handoff after design acceptance
limitations.finding: Callback API has holdings/history but no ledger/CPI/drawdown context. Capturing full future rows would violate the boundary; the accepted baseline experiment driver is hard-wired to three baseline modes and its own config hash.
limitations.requested_edit: Use a per-scenario policy state that reconstructs realized prefix wealth and prior fees from the last requested trade and next completed observation, or an explicitly tested completed-ledger observer adapter. Do not pass current outcomes or mutate accepted baseline driver. See implementation-handoff.json for partition/count/runtime estimates; chief must approve production API changes separately.
